title: Token encoder run
statement: Let $x,r$ be Boolean words. For every prefix $p$ and prior output $o$ such that $x=pr$, starting the token encoder in its token-scanning state just after $p$, with output $o$, it halts after exactly $2|a|+|b|+3$ steps with output $o$ followed by the self-delimiting encoding of $(a,b)$, where $(a,b)$ is the leading unary token and remainder obtained by splitting $r$.
hypotheses_covered: The initial scan position is $|p|$ and is within the input
replaced:
Let the unconsumed input $r$ split at its leading unary token into the
token $a$ (the maximal leading run of ones with its terminating zero, if
present) and the remainder $b$. Then, after any consumed prefix and prior
output $o$, exactly $2\abs{a} + \abs{b} + 3$ steps of the token encoder
halt with output $o$ followed by the self-delimiting pair encoding of
$(a, b)$, the final step being the blank-reading halt.
